bull_bear.body: Bonus issue recommended (1:3); Strong cash balance (INR 4,934 Mn) funding ORIGEM expansion and working capital; No debt.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: ORIGEM store-level profitability ramp-up (currently INR 15 Cr EBITDA loss for FY26); Competition in Indian lab-grown retail; US tariff policy changes (though mitigated by SEZ/US casting); Gold price volatility.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on margin expansion via hybrid casting; Aggressive on ORIGEM expansion but measured on store maturity (3-year payback); Transparent on one-offs and B2C losses.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Hybrid casting allows duty arbitrage where only Indian value-add is taxed, creating a structural moat against smaller competitors who cannot manage dual-country logistics. 64.5% of finished jewelry inventory is already with customers (consignment/stock-on-hand), smoothing future revenue recognition.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Dividend Distribution Policy aims "to maintain a minimum payout ratio of 50% of the annual Standalone PAT to be either used for Dividend and/or Buy-back of shares", with the stated objective of balancing payout against profits preserved for future growth.
- "Over the last five years (cumulative), we have delivered an average dividend pay-out of 50%+ of Standalone PAT", and "~Rs 2.5+bn distributed to shareholders via buyback and dividend over last 5 years".
- "Fortress Balance Sheet": zero net-debt structure with cash and investments exceeding Rs 4.56 Billion (June 26), stated elsewhere as Rs 4566.71 million of cash and cash equivalents including investments as at June 2026.
- "Robust free cash flow generation enables a highly disciplined capital allocation strategy, ensuring consistent, high-yield dividend distributions and continuous long-term stakeholder value creation."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: B2B Exports: 88.3% of export sales mix from lab-grown diamond jewelry; Hybrid casting in US drives continuity and margins. B2C (ORIGEM): 24 operational stores (12 opened <60 days ago), Q4 revenue INR 55.6 Mn, April sales >INR 35 Mn. Targeting 45-50 stores by FY27 exit with INR 7 Cr/month run rate.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising US tariffs on Indian jewelry imports | Goldiam International Ltd | beneficiary | High | Unique hybrid casting model (US casting + Indian finishing) minimizes duty impact to only value-add portion, unlike peers shipping fully made goods from India. |
| Consolidation of US jewelry supply chain favoring large players with US presence | Goldiam International Ltd | beneficiary | Med | Complexity of dual-casting and logistics creates barriers to entry, pushing smaller suppliers out and increasing wallet share with top US retailers. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Established in 1986, Goldiam is a premier, fully integrated manufacturer and exporter of luxury diamond jewellery" operating a "diversified, dual-engine growth model": an OEM proxy for US retail demand plus the ORIGEM domestic retail brand.
- The deck says Goldiam "has significantly transitioned from a pure natural diamond in-store jewellery company to a major supplier of Lab Grown Diamond Jewellery, with an omnichannel sales strategy".
- Claimed moat includes "complete, end-to-end ownership of the Lab-Grown Diamond value chain - from cultivation to finished jewellery export" and "deep market penetration achieved by supplying a highly targeted, fast-moving range of diamond quality to top-tier global retailers".
- ORIGEM is described as "probably India's largest COCO LGD jewellery brand; and one of the top three B2C Lab Grown Jewellery retail brand in India".
- History slide traces the shift from "commodity business of diamond manufacturing (cutting) to value added Diamond Jewellery Production & Wholesale", then to natural plus LGD jewellery export, and finally to B2C with ORIGEM.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Tariff response] Casting in the US was begun "in response to the steep hike in US tariffs", with US Product of Origin obtained "through rulings from U.S. Customs", which the deck says gives retailer customers "dependability on supply & pricing". Other income for Q1 FY2027 includes a tariff refund received by the company.
- [Gold duty] Customs duty on gold has increased to 15% (10% Basic Customs Duty plus 5% cess); the company states no material impact given its SEEPZ SEZ exemptions.
- [Acquisition] Strategic acquisition and subsequent consolidation of stake in Eco-Friendly Diamonds LLP (EDL) to 88%, giving access to supply of key raw materials for manufacturing and growing LGD.
- [Group structure] Goldiam International Limited holds Goldiam Jewellery Limited (SEEPZ, wholly owned), Goldiam USA, New York (wholly owned, marketing to retailers), Eco-Friendly Diamonds LLP (88%, growing and manufacturing lab grown diamonds) and Diagold Designs LLP.
- [Board] Rashesh Bhansali is Executive Chairman and Anmol Rashesh Bhansali is Managing Director; the board includes three independent directors and one non-executive non-independent director.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 EBITDA margin 23.9% (consolidated). Hybrid casting model expected to add 200-300 bps to gross margins annually by avoiding full duty on US-bound goods (duty only on Indian value addition). Q4 other expenses spiked due to one-offs.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Double-digit growth expected for FY27; Margin: EBITDA margins expected to expand further in FY27 (full year benefit of hybrid casting), incremental gross margin impact of 200-300 bps; Order Inflow: Robust demand in US bridal and new fashion segments; Capex/Commissioning: ORIGEM expansion to 45-50 stores by FY27 exit.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into high-ASP fashion jewelry (tennis bracelets/necklaces) in B2B; Scaling ORIGEM to 50 stores with mature store revenue target of INR 35-40 Lakhs/month; Sales enablers like 360 Ring Builder and old gold exchange.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Goldiam crossed INR 1,000 Cr revenue with record PAT, driven by a 'hybrid casting' model that mitigates US tariffs and expands margins by 200-300 bps. While B2B exports remain robust, the key growth optionality lies in scaling ORIGEM retail stores to 50 by FY27 end, targeting double-digit consolidated growth despite current B2C losses.

open.item: Board recommended a 1:3 bonus issue (one new Rs.2 share for every three existing Rs.2 shares), subject to shareholder approval.
8 to 10 more ORIGEM stores are coming up, all operational by September 2026 (from 24 currently).
ORIGEM is adding sales enablers: a 360 3D digital ring builder (India-first, already live), plus upcoming old-gold exchange, purchase plans, 9KT gold and a possible silver line.
ORIGEM marketing spend budgeted at Rs.4-4.5 crores for H1 FY27.
Management targets 45-50 COCO ORIGEM stores by exit FY27, possibly with a quarter focused on ramping existing store revenue.
Management targets an ORIGEM exit revenue of about Rs.7 crores per month for FY27.
Management is looking forward to positive double-digit total-company revenue growth in FY27 over the record FY26 base.
Management expects the FY27 margin profile to be significantly stronger and higher than Q4 FY26, driven by a full year of the dual/hybrid US casting model (200-300 bps gross-margin increment).
Company will introduce high-ASP fashion jewellery (tennis bracelets and tennis necklaces) in the coming year to expand the addressable market and lift ASP.
Management aims to control/contain the overall ORIGEM loss even while doubling to ~50 stores, using older stores' profits to subsidize newer stores.

ORIGEM store cost ~Rs.3.5 crores (Rs.2.5cr inventory) with store-level breakeven at Rs.17-19 lakhs/month, targeting breakeven within 6-9 months and ~3-year payback at maturity (~Rs.35-45 lakhs/month).
Sanctions on Russia/ALROSA are causing non-availability of rough natural diamonds and higher natural diamond prices, slowing retailer orders.
